title: The definition of a strongly connected component omits maximality.
details: Lovett/Shen, CSE200 Lecture 6, 2013-04-17, Definition 2, printed 6-1 (PDF p.1). The stated condition requires only pairwise mutual reachability in A. It omits maximality, so it also holds for either singleton in a two-vertex directed cycle although both vertices belong to one strongly connected component. Arbitrary subsets satisfying the printed condition do not give the asserted component quotient. Repair: define components as equivalence classes of mutual reachability (allowing length-zero paths), or require maximal nonempty mutually reachable subsets. This preserves the implication-graph criterion and the reverse-order assignment proof. The adopted treatment in two-satisfiability#mutual-components defines whole equivalence classes of mutual reachability and uses their genuine quotient partial order, repairing the omission.
